comments.author: vhantz
comments.textRawHtml:
Schrödinger's China at once is an evil entity looking to use AI for their own nefarious purposes yet also willing to cooperate with their main competitor to prevent other actors (who??) from achieving similar goals (all while under a chip embargo too!!)

The reality is much less confusing: Anthropic CEO does not wish for models with similar (or greater) capabilities compared to his own closed and overpriced ones to be widely released. Simply because that will affect Anthropic's bottom-line.

Anthropic and all other "model" companies have nothing making them special beyond privileged access to chips so obviously they want to restrict what models are out there and more importantly who can produce new ones. Without these restrictions, it's only a matter of time before the multi-hundred billions valuations simply evaporate while they are still holding the bag.
comments.textZhHtml:
薛定谔的中国，一方面被描绘成企图利用AI实现其险恶目的的邪恶实体，另一方面又被说成愿意与主要竞争对手合作，以阻止其他行为体（谁？？）实现类似目标（而且这一切还是在芯片禁运之下！！）

现实远没有那么令人困惑：Anthropic CEO只是不希望那些与其自家闭源且定价过高的模型能力相当（甚至更强）的模型被广泛发布。原因很简单，这会直接影响Anthropic的利润。

Anthropic和其他所有“模型”公司，除了享有获取芯片的特权外，根本没有什么特别之处，所以他们显然想要限制市面上有哪些模型，更重要的是限制谁能开发新模型。如果没有这些限制，他们还在高位站岗时，那数千亿美元的估值化为泡影就只是时间问题了。

Incentive and ability are what should be looked at. There, things get far more interesting: what is the current state of AI employed by the US intelligence agencies and what do they use it for?

stories.title: US citizen charged after GrapheneOS phone wipes during airport search
stories.titleZh: 美国公民在机场搜查期间擦拭 GrapheneOS 手机后被指控

comments.author: schoen
comments.textRawHtml:
I co-wrote a border search guide for EFF some years ago. I was very interested in finding clever technical approaches but I later ended up feeling that I hadn't given enough thought to the overall threat model questions (even though the guide did address them, perhaps even somewhat usefully).

The big picture problem is that the agents performing the searches have an enormous amount of power in terms of potentially seizing devices and potentially denying entry for non-citizens. I think they should not have this power, but the agents and courts probably don't care that I think that.

The end result (not inherently different from what we wrote in the guide) is that you may have to think both about protecting your data by technical means, and about not angering the agents more than you plan to. I was fascinated by techniques for being unable to comply (which is straightforward to achieve if you want!) but probably didn't think enough about how much this might antagonize border agents in many cases.

I definitely don't know a comprehensive big-picture solution.
comments.textZhHtml:
几年前，我与他人共同为 EFF 编写了一份边境搜索指南。我对寻找巧妙的技术方法非常感兴趣，但后来我发现我没有对整体威胁模型问题给予足够的考虑（尽管指南确实解决了这些问题，甚至可能有些有用）。

大局问题是，执行搜索的特工拥有巨大的权力，可能会扣押设备并可能拒绝非公民进入。我认为他们不应该拥有这种权力，但代理人和法院可能并不关心我的想法。

最终结果（与我们在指南中编写的内容没有本质上的不同）是，您可能必须考虑通过技术手段保护您的数据，并且不要比您计划的更激怒代理人。我对无法遵守规定的技术很着迷（如果你愿意的话，这很容易实现！），但可能没有充分考虑到在许多情况下这可能会在多大程度上激怒边境人员。

我绝对不知道一个全面的整体解决方案。

children.author: lentil_soup
children.textRawHtml:
> you may have to think both about protecting your data by technical means, and about not angering the agents more than you plan to

That's the same problem with technical solutions to crime.

I come from a very dangerous city and I used to have a car that needed a PIN to work. You could turn then engine on and drive but after a minute if you didn't input the PIN it would turn off without warning and start blasting the alarm. The idea being that if the car was stolen the thief would be stranded not far from home unsure about what's happening. Great technical solution but it ignores that a lot of the time the car is stolen with you in it (in a kidnapping, for example). Having the car shutoff in the middle of a highway next to a panicking guy with a gun and trying to remember a PIN is not a situation you want to be in, so I just had the PIN number written down on the dashboard, which worked very well when I was eventually kidnapped and just pointed at the piece of paper with the number.
children.textZhHtml:
> 您可能必须考虑通过技术手段保护您的数据，并且不要超出您计划地激怒特工

这对于犯罪的技术解决方案来说也是同样的问题。

我来自一个非常危险的城市，我曾经有一辆需要 PIN 码才能工作的汽车。然后你可以打开引擎并驾驶，但一分钟后，如果你没有输入 PIN 码，它就会在没有警告的情况下关闭并开始发出警报。这个想法是，如果汽车被盗，小偷就会被困在离家不远的地方，不确定发生了什么。很棒的技术解决方案，但它忽略了很多时候汽车在你开着的情况下被盗（例如，在绑架中）。在高速公路中间，汽车被关闭，旁边是一个持枪的惊慌失措的人，并试图记住 PIN 码，这不是你想要的情况，所以我只是将 PIN 码写在仪表板上，当我最终被绑架时，只需指着一张带有数字的纸，这非常有效。

Again in phone terms, maybe bring a blank phone through that border.

用手机术语来说，这就是 5 美元扳手的问题。如果您可以简单地以某种方式强制绕过它，那么复杂的技术就没有意义。

children.author: ryanbrunner
children.textRawHtml:
A blank phone is suspicious in and of itself and probably invites more questioning and suspicion.

And from personal experience, once a border guard is suspicious of you and you're a non-citizen, you're fighting a losing battle to get into that country, regardless of whether you're doing anything shady / illegal.

The most straightforward answer I think is to use common apps for more commonplace social media activities and separate apps that can be removed from your phone when you're crossing a border for things you want to keep private. It's not perfect privacy, but I think a border is one thing that for better or worse you'll need to accept some compromises on.
children.textZhHtml:
一部空白的手机本身就十分可疑，很可能会招来更多的盘问和怀疑。

根据我的个人经验，一旦边防人员对你产生怀疑，而你又非该国公民，那么无论你是否有从事任何不可告人或违法的活动，想要入境该国都注定是徒劳的。

我认为最直接的解决办法是，用常规应用处理日常的社交媒体活动，而对于想要保密的内容，则使用单独的应用，并在过境时将其从手机中卸载。这算不上完美的隐私保护，但我认为在过边境这件事上，无论好坏，你都不得不做出一些妥协。

That is a largely incorrect statement that is loosely based on a single incident, not a trend.

The single incident was an individual in Malaysia who added an after-market finger-print based engine immobilizer to his car in 2005. The attackers threatened the individual with machetes, so that he would put his finger on the sensor, and then drove off with him in the car. The attackers later cut off his finger believing it would let them restart it without him present.

It will be very interesting to see what kind of 'slow' performance people get from running it on a no GPU, but tons of RAM server (like a dual or quad socket xeon with 1.5 to 3TB of RAM). For the purpose of giving it longer duration tasks to generate a piece of something and come back and check on what it has done in 4 or 6 hours. Even if the output is like 5-6 tok/s, that might be usable for some purposes.

Huge price difference in what you can do with buying a used 4U rackmount server and putting 3TB of RAM in it (64GB DIMMs x quantity 32 in a quad socket xeon, you can see some benchmark prices on eBay for sets of 16 or 32 matched 64GB ECC DIMMs) for <$30,000, vs the cost of trying to run it on real GPU hardware.

Now obviously, as of the time I write this, the full precision hasn't been released nor has anyone like unsloth run it through quantization yet to produce a "Q8" or "Q8-XL" variant of it. But I think it's going to need more than 1536GB of RAM, with a usable and large amount of context, more like 2TB and preferably 2.5 to 3TB.

I also predict that people who try to run it in Q4 and Q6 will get the worst of both worlds, less precision/lost knowledge but also not reliable output that comes out too slow. In my personal opinion if I'm going to deal with something that is smart but slow and running on limited budget hardware, I need it to be Q8.

My point is that the tradeoff to get off-peak pricing is that on-peak is way, way more expensive. So you can charge the EV off-peak to maximize the savings, but everything else you do during on-peak time costs way more.

Using myself as an example:

I adjust my A/C to run outside of 5pm-9pm (peak) if at all possible, we try to avoid pointless high-draw usage during that same window, and both of our EVs hold off charging until after 9pm.

My rate from 5pm-9pm is 0.43/kWh. My rate after 9pm is 0.09/kWh. The flat rate alternative, if I did not want to worry about time of day, would be 0.21/kWh. These prices are all-in, including transmission and distribution/whatever.

It would be dishonest to say that my EVs only cost me 0.09/kWh to operate, which on it's face is a claim to paying over 50% less. In reality, time of day pricing typically saves me somewhere between 10% and 15% in an average month compared with flat rate.

如果可能的话，我将空调调整为在下午 5 点至晚上 9 点（高峰）之外运行，我们尽量避免在同一时间段内无意义的高消耗使用，并且我们的两辆电动汽车都将充电推迟到晚上 9 点之后。

我下午 5 点至晚上 9 点的费率是0.43/千瓦时。 我晚上 9 点后的电价是 0.09/kWh。 如果我不想担心一天中的时间，统一费率替代方案为 0.21/kWh。 这些价格是全部价格，包括输电和配电等。

If you leave the EV charging out of your consumption, does a time of day plan still save you money on the remaining usage? Or does it cost you? If it saves you money, then it would make sense to be on a ToD plan regardless of EV charging. Which means it makes sense to consider your additional EV draw as costing the marginal off-peak rate. Essentially the EV load has the valuable property of being dispatchable.

You can do the same thought experiment with say a dehumidifier in your basement. It can easily be off during peak usage and still accomplish its job, so its cost of electricity is also the marginal off-peak rate.

comments.author: squidbeak
comments.textRawHtml:
I've limited sympathy for the publishers.

It pisses me off to reflect that they can sit on works until copyright expires, keeping them out of print. There's no real need for any of these so-called rare books to be rare while they're under copyright.

And related to this, the books that are in print are mostly only in print in the shittiest way. I often see well-made books from the 17th or 18th centuries which are still in good nick. It's ridiculous that in the 21st century, publication standards have fallen to the point where for most works a disposable format is the only type available - where no amount of money could buy a truly decent hardback copy.

If we have to have copyright laws, I'd like to see two changes to them.

When a publisher has no incentive to keep an edition in print, it should be available to any other publisher to print, without compensation to the original publisher, and with renegotiated royalties for the author.

And if the publisher keeps a book in print - but only in bestseller-grade materials, bogroll paper that furrows in any humidity and perfect binding that molts its pages a couple of dry seasons later - and if it refuses to print a durable hardback copy with signatures, good paper and decent print - something that will still be readable in several generations' time - any other publisher keen to have a crack at it should be able to, again without any compensation for the original publisher, though perhaps in this case, with matching royalties for the author.
comments.textZhHtml:

与此相关的是，那些还在印的书大多印得烂透了。我经常看到17或18世纪制作精良的书，至今保存完好。可笑的是，在21世纪，出版标准竟然沦落到大多数作品只能以快消式装帧出版的地步——花多少钱都买不到一本真正像样的精装书。

如果我们非得有版权法，我希望看到两项修改。

当出版商没有动力让某个版本继续加印时，应允许任何其他出版商印刷，无需向原出版商支付补偿，并与作者重新协商版税。

如果出版商让一本书保持在售——但只用畅销书级别的劣质材料，那种一遇潮气就起皱的卫生纸级纸张，还有过两个旱季就掉页的胶装——而且拒绝印刷耐用的精装本，不用锁线装订、好纸和好油墨——那种能流传几代人依然清晰可读的版本——那么任何想尝试出版的其他出版商都应该被允许这样做，同样无需向原出版商支付任何补偿，不过在这种情况下，或许可以给作者同等版税。

children.author: constantius
children.textRawHtml:
To your second point: a company (or any kind of organisation) is continuous work. It's a very obvious retort to your analogy. It would be akin to the author writing a book in a series every year for twenty years, then giving their rights to their child who keeps writing books every year, and every book only has 20 years of copyright. Seems fair to me.

To your first point: inheritance has a concentrating effect on wealth. Concentration of wealth is not a good thing, as it breeds inequality by definition.

If your grandparents gave you a house for free, and you used that enormous advantage to pur your money elsewhere and then own 2, 3 houses, and your child then gets 10, that's 10 houses that people could own themselves, instead of paying the highest rent that your child can get away with.

If you have any experience of poverty, you should understand how viscerally unfair the existence of 'rich kids' seem, and how damaging it is to society.
children.textZhHtml:
关于第二点：公司（或任何类型的组织）是持续不断的工作。这是对你的类比的非常明显的反驳。这就好比作者在二十年里每年写一本系列书，然后把权利交给自己的孩子，孩子每年都继续写书，而每本书只有20年的版权。对我来说似乎很公平。

对于你的第一点：继承对财富有集中作用。财富集中不是一件好事，因为它本质上会滋生不平等。

如果你的祖父母免费给你一套房子，而你利用这种巨大优势将钱转移到其他地方，然后拥有 2、3 套房子，你的孩子就得到 10 套，这就是人们可以拥有的 10 套房子，而不是支付你的孩子可以逃脱的最高租金。

如果你有过贫困经历，你应该明白“富家子弟”的存在在本质上是多么不公平，以及它对社会的危害有多大。

children.author: altmanaltman
children.textRawHtml:
> To your second point: a company (or any kind of organisation) is continuous work. It's a very obvious retort to your analogy. It would be akin to the author writing a book in a series every year for twenty years, then giving their rights to their child who keeps writing books every year, and every book only has 20 years of copyright. Seems fair to me.

I don't understand how that is fair though? Why should the author give away their rights without any compensation to the public is my point. Continous work is not really relevant to this, otherwise you would have concede that any previous work done by the company in 20 years including their trademarks, logos, ideas should be free for the public to use? Otherwise it is clearly unfair that we treat writers with one set of law regarding property but have another set of laws for every other business?

And yes, capitalism is not good but my point is that it supports inheritance as a system. It doesn't care where you got the money. Is it fair? Of course not. The root of this is based on exploitation and it is what the world has accepted as the common form of economy.

And yes, I have experienced poverty but I don't think its viscerally unfair that "rich kids" exist. Why is it unfair in an objective term? Because they got handed things for free? Or because they have it better than you? In either case, it would be very easy to find examples of people who have it 10 times worse than you and who think your existence is unfair. But is it really?

> If your grandparents gave you a house for free, and you used that enormous advantage to pur your money elsewhere and then own 2, 3 houses, and your child then gets 10, that's 10 houses that people could own themselves, instead of paying the highest rent that your child can get away with.

Or you could also lose all your money by being stupid with it and not having any skills. If you have the skill to build upon the foundation, why is it luck? Why are we assuming just because your grandparents gave you a house for free, you'll automatically continue to build upon it and not lose it (which happens a lot more often than you would think). Should that skill not be respected? Who are you to determine what is fair and what is not.
children.textZhHtml:
> 关于第二点：公司（或任何类型的组织）是持续工作的。这是对你的类比的非常明显的反驳。这就好比作者在二十年里每年写一本系列书，然后把权利交给自己的孩子，孩子每年都继续写书，而每本书只有20年的版权。对我来说似乎很公平。

我不明白这怎么公平？为什么作者要放弃自己的权利而不向公众提供任何补偿，这是我的观点。连续工作与此并不真正相关，否则你会承认公司在 20 年内所做的任何先前工作，包括他们的商标、徽标、想法都应该免费供公众使用？否则，我们用一套关于财产的法律对待作家，但对其他所有行业都有另一套法律，这显然是不公平的？

是的，资本主义不好，但我的观点是，它支持继承作为一种制度。它并不关心你从哪里得到钱。公平吗？当然不是。其根源是基于剥削，这是世界所接受的普遍经济形式。

是的，我经历过贫困，但我不认为“富家子弟”的存在本质上是不公平的。为什么说客观上不公平呢？因为他们免费得到东西？还是因为他们比你拥有更好的东西？无论哪种情况，都很容易找到比你糟糕十倍并且认为你的存在不公平的人的例子。但真的是这样吗？

>如果你的祖父母免费给了你一套房子，你利用这个巨大的优势在别处花钱，然后拥有2、3套房子，然后你的孩子得到10套，那就是人们可以自己拥有的10套房子，而不是支付你的孩子可以逃脱的最高租金。

或者你也可能因为愚蠢而没有任何技能而损失所有的钱。如果你有能力在基础上再接再厉，为什么还要运气呢？为什么我们假设仅仅因为你的祖父母免费给了你一套房子，你就会自动地继续在它的基础上建造而不是失去它（这种情况发生的频率比你想象的要高得多）。这种技能不应该受到尊重吗？你是谁来决定什么是公平的，什么是不公平的。

children.author: monknomo
children.textRawHtml:
So what? Why should the state grant you a monopoly at all?

The reason is to encourage people to create useful writings and make useful discoveries. But we need to balance this encouragement with the benefit we get by making these writings and discoveries available to everyone. By granting a time-bound monopoly the state rewards creators, and by ensuring this time period is not excessive, spreads the benefit among the populace.

Plus, with a time bound benefit, you have to keep on creating, which is good for everyone under this regime.

These aren't, like, inherent rights, they are contingent
children.textZhHtml:
那又怎样？国家凭什么要授予你垄断权呢？

其目的是鼓励人们创作有益的作品并做出有用的发现。但我们必须将这种鼓励与让所有人共享这些作品和发现所带来的利益进行平衡。通过授予有期限的垄断权，国家奖励了创作者；同时通过确保这一期限不会过长，将利益惠及大众。

此外，由于这种利益是有期限的，你就必须不断进行创作，这对该制度下的所有人都有好处。

这些权利并非什么与生俱来的权利，而是有条件的。

children.author: altmanaltman
children.textRawHtml: The point isn't why the state should grant me (or writers) a monopoly. But rather, why should the principle not be applied to all property and ownership and not just copyright for creative works? Why should one lose ownership over their said work if they are a writer but they shouldn't lose ownership of their trade secrets because they are a high-frequency trader? Or more so, why should only the creative field worry about the public better good when it comes to ownership and property? The conversation for public domain must extend to everything and not just works or art if one really believes in it.
children.textZhHtml: 问题不在于为什么国家应该授予我（或作家）垄断权。相反，为什么该原则不应适用于所有财产和所有权，而不仅仅是创意作品的版权？如果一个人是一名作家，为什么要失去对其上述作品的所有权，但他们不应该因为是一名高频交易员而失去其商业秘密的所有权？或者更重要的是，为什么只有创意领域才应该在所有权和财产方面担心公共利益？如果人们真正相信公共领域，那么公共领域的对话必须扩展到一切，而不仅仅是作品或艺术。

children.author: lsaferite
children.textRawHtml: Funny that you are comparing Copyrights and Trade Secrets. The monopoly granted on Copyright is predicated on it being published. Trade Secrets, by definition, are not published. Copyright is granted based on the value to the public provided by the author publishing their works. Trade Secrets have no such protection as they are not meant for the public good. They have other protection from theft, but once they are published, there is no protection of the information.
children.textZhHtml: 有趣的是，您正在比较版权和商业秘密。对版权的垄断是以它的出版为基础的。根据定义，商业秘密是不公开的。版权的授予是基于作者发布其作品为公众提供的价值。商业秘密没有这样的保护，因为它们不是为了公共利益。它们有其他防盗保护措施，但一旦发布，就没有信息保护。

stories.title: How is the Bun rewrite in Rust going?
stories.titleZh: Bun 用 Rust 重写的进展如何？

comments.author: Jarred
comments.textRawHtml:
Bun’s Rust rewrite shipped in Claude Code over a month ago and barely anyone noticed. Claude Code is widely used. The Rust rewrite is going well overall.

In the Bun v1.4 video, I promised a certain number of newly passing Node.js tests were added to force us to improve compatibility, and that number is not true yet. The release is delayed until it is true. The PRs to make it true are up but not merged yet. Most likely next Tuesday we’ll do the release of 1.4.
comments.textZhHtml:
Bun 的 Rust 重写在一个多月前在 Claude Code 中发布，但几乎没有人注意到。克劳德码被广泛使用。 Rust 重写总体进展顺利。

在 Bun v1.4 视频中，我承诺添加一定数量的新通过的 Node.js 测试来迫使我们提高兼容性，但这个数字还不是真的。发布时间将被推迟，直到消息属实为止。实现这一目标的 PR 已发布，但尚未合并。我们很可能会在下周二发布 1.4。

children.author: inglor
children.textRawHtml:
Take as long as you need to ensure software quality. A month without a release isn't a big deal and whomever needs a specific feature can offer to contribute or build themselves.

Node has 4-6 weeks without a meaningful release (other than security stuff) pretty much every December. I think the criticism in the article is unfounded and whomever needed/wanted a release should have asked first instead of writing an "angry" blog post.

(I'm a Node.js maintainer)
children.textZhHtml:
只要您需要，就可以确保软件质量。一个月没有发布版本并不是什么大问题，任何需要特定功能的人都可以贡献或构建自己。

Node 几乎每年 12 月都会有 4-6 周没有发布有意义的版本（安全性内容除外）。我认为文章中的批评是没有根据的，任何需要/想要发布的人都应该先提出要求，而不是写一篇“愤怒”的博客文章。

（我是 Node.js 维护者）

children.textRawHtml:

children.author: kelseyfrog

You have to stop thinking like an engineer and start thinking like a public health official.

'Something impossible for kids to bypass' is not the goal. It's akin to evaluating a flu vaccine on the standard of zero breakthrough cases. Such a standard has no relevance on the efficacy of the vaccine.

Likewise for underage internet access. Proponents would be happily satisfied with 90% compliance. They really don't care that coverage isn't complete or circumvention is complete. Once you realize that, you can start constructing counterarguments that dismantle the claim that digital IDs would solve the problems they're supposed to.

children.author: cykros
children.textRawHtml:
Kids can't bypass it because the systems they're trying to access are entirely different than they were in 1995. They are not accessing "the Internet" on which they connect to their friend's BBS's, irc servers, Usenet, etc. They're large, private systems which can absolutely be locked down by the parties that own them, on which activity has largely been centered.

Kids CAN absolutely bypass a lot still. Jump on Nostr and nobody can stop anyone -- a server can be run on any device (mine is on my phone), and it'll even run on non-TCP/IP networks (FIPS is in early days and still largely runs on existing infrastructure but absolutely doesn't rely on it staying there). Give it another few months with some LoRA build out (and enough motivation for the kids) and even the ISP gateway stops being a filter point. Not that ISP level controls have ever really been the most effective anyway, given the existence of VPN's and other tunneling methods (to say nothing of public wifi networks).

We see this happening in real time as India tries to stamp out Bitchat. The codebase has appeared on more and more repositories, and the most recent version of Bitchat is capable of transmitting itself for install to other devies without relying on any server or Internet at all.

So should we push back? Of course. At some point we would need to worry that they'll say enough is enough and make the hardware itself inaccessible. We're a long way off from that, and it'd be a surefire way to get a LOT more pushback.

But in the meantime, we shouldn't despair too much. The cypherpunks that gave us private and secure access on the Internet used by everyone today despite being once illegal to export didn't go anywhere. They're still here, kicking down every wall that gets put up, or at least pointing out that there are multiple ways around (or through) it.
children.textZhHtml:
孩子们无法绕过它，因为他们尝试访问的系统与 1995 年完全不同。他们不再访问连接到朋友的 BBS、irc 服务器、Usenet 等的“互联网”。它们是大型的私有系统，绝对可以被拥有它们的各方锁定，而活动主要集中在该系统上。

孩子们绝对可以绕过很多东西。跳上Nostr，没有人可以阻止任何人——服务器可以在任何设备上运行（我的在我的手机上），它甚至可以在非TCP/IP网络上运行（FIPS还处于早期阶段，仍然主要在现有基础设施上运行，但绝对不依赖于它停留在那里）。再过几个月，进行一些 LoRA 构建（并为孩子们提供足够的动力），甚至 ISP 网关也不再是过滤点。无论如何，考虑到 VPN 和其他隧道方法（更不用说公共 WiFi 网络）的存在，ISP 级别的控制实际上并不是最有效的。

当印度试图消灭 Bitchat 时，我们实时看到这种情况发生。代码库已经出现在越来越多的存储库中，并且最新版本的 Bitchat 能够自行传输以安装到其他设备，而根本不依赖任何服务器或互联网。

那么我们应该推迟吗？当然。在某些时候，我们需要担心他们会说够了，导致硬件本身无法访问。我们离这个目标还有很长的路要走，这肯定会遭到更多的阻力。

但与此同时，我们不应该太绝望。尽管曾经非法出口，但密码朋克为我们提供了当今每个人都使用的私密且安全的互联网访问权限，但它们却没有去任何地方。他们仍然在这里，踢倒每一堵墙，或者至少指出有多种方法可以绕过（或穿过）它。

children.author: yorwba
children.textRawHtml:
The last time I had police knocking at my door, it was a lot more than two, and they were readying their battering ram when I opened, and then immediately swarmed me and told me to sit down, and then I just explained and they realized their warrant was for a different address and they left. It was scary in the moment, but I never had a gun pointed at me and I wasn't even touched, so overall it left me with a rather positive impression of how search warrants are executed in Germany.

By all means, if you have an adversarial relationship with the state, fight every expansion of its power tooth and nail. But conversely, if you think that everything is going basically fine and the police are reasonable folks overall, then giving them more power doesn't look like a slippery slope straight to dystopia.
children.textZhHtml:

无论如何，如果你与国家有敌对关系，请坚决抵制其权力的每一次扩张。但相反，如果你认为一切都基本顺利，而且警察总体上都是通情达理的人，那么赋予他们更多权力看起来并不像是直接通往反乌托邦的滑坡。

children.author: nate_meurer
children.textRawHtml:
> giving them more power doesn't look like a slippery slope straight to dystopia.

This only makes sense if you have no concept of "future", wherein different, less reasonable people can gain power. This should be especially obvious in Germany, where an adversarial relationship with the state can easily be had by merely criticizing it.
children.textZhHtml:
> 赋予他们更多权力看起来并不会直接滑向反乌托邦的深渊。

这种说法只有在你对“未来”毫无概念的情况下才成立，因为在未来，不同且不那么理智的人可能会掌权。这在德国应该尤为明显，在那里，仅仅因为批评国家就可能与国家形成对立关系。

children.author: yorwba
children.textRawHtml:
On the contrary, I don't think the current relative lack of arbitrary police brutality depends on the reasonableness of the people in power at all, only on the reasonableness of individual police officers. The police don't suddenly get softer when there's a left-wing government in power and tougher when there's a right-wing government.

That "merely criticizing" the state gets you into an adversarial relationship is, I think, also overblown. For example, insulting someone is a crime in Germany. This is usually not enforced on children's playgrounds, so many remain unaware of this until adulthood. Then they might insult someone who is aware of the law (e.g. a representative of the state) in public and get surprised by a lawsuit. Similarly, spray-painting slogans on someone's house without permission will get prosecuted as vandalism. But if you stick to publishing in ways that normal people publish pro-state opinions, you can publish your criticism in the same way and nobody will bat an eye. (Certainly, a large number of people are criticizing the state in exactly this way at any given time, without being worse off for it.)
children.textZhHtml:
相反，我认为目前相对缺乏任意警察暴行的情况，根本不取决于掌权者的理智程度，而只取决于个别警察的理智程度。当左翼政府执政时，警察不会突然变得温和，右翼政府执政时也不会突然变得强硬。

我认为，所谓“仅仅批评”国家就会让你陷入对立关系的说法也被夸大了。例如，在德国侮辱他人是犯罪行为。这通常不会在儿童游乐场执行，所以许多人直到成年都不知道这一点。然后他们可能会在公共场合侮辱了解法律的人（比如国家代表），结果被一纸诉状搞得措手不及。同样，未经允许在别人房子上喷漆写标语会被作为破坏公物起诉。但如果你坚持用普通人发表亲政府言论的方式来发表批评，你也可以用同样的方式发表批评，没人会多看一眼。（当然，在任何时候，都有大量的人以这种方式批评国家，而且他们的处境并没有因此变得更糟。）

children.author: wasabi991011
children.textRawHtml:
> The police don't suddenly get softer when there's a left-wing government in power and tougher when there's a right-wing government.

They absolutely can though, through hiring selection bias, training, firing, promotion criteria, bonuses, performance metrics and quotas, oversight enforcement or lack thereof, etc. It's not quick, but incentive structures can absolutely change an organizational culture.
children.textZhHtml:
> 警方不会仅仅因为左翼政府执政就突然变得温和，也不会因为右翼政府执政就突然变得强硬。

但实际上完全可以，通过招聘时的选拔偏见、培训、解雇、晋升标准、奖金、绩效指标和配额、监督执行与否等方式。这并非一蹴而就，但激励机制绝对能改变一个组织的文化。

It's not necessarily corruption. If there's no conflict between principal and agent, it's fine.

Just like when I sent my butler to go and buy a bottle of wine, he can make arbitrary choices, but that doesn't mean he's corrupt or going against my wishes. I trust his judgement, and since it's a repeated game our incentives are aligned.
children.textZhHtml:
> 你说“文化契合”，我说“腐败”，让我们彻底解决这个问题。

这不一定是腐败。 如果委托人和代理人之间没有冲突就可以了。

就像我派管家去买一瓶酒一样，他可以随意选择，但这并不意味着他腐败或违背我的意愿。 我相信他的判断，而且由于这是一个重复的游戏，我们的动机是一致的。

children.author: marcosdumay
children.textRawHtml: If the company got any investment, than the principal has no interest in "cultural fit" and it's always corruption.
children.textZhHtml: 如果公司获得了任何投资，那么资方就不会对“文化契合度”感兴趣，那永远都是腐败。

children.author: sneak
children.textRawHtml:
It’s not corruption to simply hire the people you subjectively feel a preference for working for, instead of objective criteria. It’s not public tax funds that fuel salaries, it’s your own money. You get to spend it how you like.

Yes, many jurisdictions have outlawed arbitrary discrimination against protected classes (eg race), which is an entirely different matter, and not what we are discussing here.
children.textZhHtml:
仅仅根据主观偏好而非客观标准来雇佣你想共事的人，这算不上腐败。支付薪水的不是公共税收，而是你自己的钱。你想怎么花就怎么花。

是的，许多司法管辖区已经取缔了针对受保护阶层（如种族）的任意歧视，但这完全是另一回事，也不是我们在这里讨论的内容。

stories.title: A missing underscore sent innocent man to prison for 18 months

comments.author: Aurornis
comments.textRawHtml:
> Nothing linked Klayme to the girl. No intimate images were found. Klayme did have a Kik account, but cops couldn’t even show that he had accessed the service during the period in question.

> Still, Klayme was arrested and hit with three charges:

> Luring a person under 14 years of age by means of telecommunication

> Providing sexually explicit material to a child

> Possession of child pornography

> The case went to trial, where Klayme was found guilty. He then went to prison for 18 months.

What in the world happened in this case?

How can someone be convicted of these charges without any evidence?

Unless the article left something out, the only possible evidence they had was the wrong username. They couldn't even find evidence that this person used Kik at the time of the crime.

What defense did his lawyer even try? I'm so confused.
comments.textZhHtml:
> 没有任何证据将克莱姆与那个女孩联系起来。没有发现亲密照片。 Klayme 确实有一个 Kik 帐户，但警方甚至无法证明他在相关期间访问过该服务。

> 尽管如此，Klayme 仍被捕并被指控三项罪名：

> 通过电信手段引诱 14 岁以下的人

> 向儿童提供露骨色情材料

> 持有儿童色情制品

> 该案进入审判阶段，Klayme 被判有罪。然后他入狱了 18 个月。

这起案件到底发生了什么？

在没有任何证据的情况下，怎么能被定罪？

除非文章遗漏了什么，否则他们唯一可能的证据就是错误的用户名。他们甚至找不到此人在犯罪时使用 Kik 的证据。

他的律师甚至尝试过什么辩护？我很困惑。

children.author: shusaku
children.textRawHtml: It all comes down to the jury, none of those things matter. The bigger issue here: he knew those messages weren’t him, so the lawyer should’ve gone full force to figure out how this happened. I would guess his lawyer didn’t really believe him
children.textZhHtml: 这一切都取决于陪审团，这些都不重要。这里更大的问题是：他知道这些信息不是他发的，所以律师应该全力以赴弄清楚这是怎么发生的。我猜他的律师并不真正相信他

children.author: thephyber
children.textRawHtml:
It was a judge, not a jury.

And yeah, the trial lawyer failed to make the case, but if the defendant couldn't raise money for a defense, they he likely didn't have any experts to refute the prosecution's evidence.
children.textZhHtml:
这是法官，而不是陪审团。

是的，主审律师未能立案，但如果被告无法筹集辩护资金，他们很可能没有任何专家来反驳检方的证据。

children.author: qingcharles
children.textRawHtml: I don't know about the Canadian justice system, but it's very hard in the USA for defendants to get expert witnesses. The state is supposed to pay, but it's almost never done, and when it is they pay bottom rate for the defendant while having unlimited funds for their own experts.
children.textZhHtml: 我不了解加拿大的司法系统，但在美国，被告很难找到专家证人。国家应该支付费用，但几乎从未这样做过，当支付费用时，他们为被告支付最低费率，同时为自己的专家提供无限的资金。

children.author: OsrsNeedsf2P
children.textRawHtml:
Oh something I can comment on!

A friend of mine was facing a mountain of criminal charges. Photo evidence proved the cops lied. We needed an expert testimony explaining the camera angle and why the photo explained how the cops lied.

I think we called every service qualified for providing such a testimony in Ontario, and a good portion of them across all of Canada. Some were even happy to work with us, until they found out we were testifying against the police. We ended up going international but without luck, and ended up with no expert testimony
children.textZhHtml:
哦，我可以发表评论！

我的一个朋友面临着大量的刑事指控。照片证据证明警察撒了谎。我们需要一份专家证词来解释拍摄角度以及为什么照片解释了警察如何撒谎。

我认为我们称安大略省所有有资格提供此类证词的服务机构，以及加拿大各地的大部分服务机构。有些人甚至很乐意与我们合作，直到他们发现我们在作证指控警方。我们最终走向国际，但运气不佳，最终没有专家证言

children.author: pinkmuffinere
children.textRawHtml:
> I think we called every service qualified for providing such a testimony in Ontario, and a good portion of them across all of Canada. Some were even happy to work with us, until they found out we were testifying against the police. We ended up going international but without luck, and ended up with no expert testimony

This is absolutely horrible to hear!! I know you probably don't want homework, but would you ever consider taking this story to news outlets? I suspect there'd be no compensation, but the uproar might (eventually) result in change.
children.textZhHtml:
> 我认为我们称安大略省所有有资格提供此类证词的服务机构，以及加拿大各地的大部分服务机构。有些人甚至很乐意与我们合作，直到他们发现我们在作证指控警方。我们最终走向国际，但运气不佳，最终没有专家证词

这绝对是可怕的消息！我知道你可能不想做作业，但你会考虑把这个故事带到新闻媒体吗？我怀疑不会有任何补偿，但骚动可能（最终）导致改变。

children.author: leni536
children.textRawHtml: This is insane. I guess this is because of economic incentives, and expert witnesses risk losing work coming from prosecutors if they ever testify against them?
children.textZhHtml: 这太疯狂了。我想这是因为经济动机，如果专家证人作证反对他们，他们就有可能失去检察官的工作？

children.author: thephyber
children.textRawHtml:
Interesting.

I was actually dismissed from a jury panel partially because I said I don't know if I could trust the experts because my perception is that individual experts either repeatedly testify for only the prosecution or only the defense.
children.textZhHtml:
有趣。

我实际上被陪审团开除，部分原因是我说我不知道我是否可以信任专家，因为我的看法是，个别专家要么反复只为控方作证，要么只为辩方作证。

children.author: e40
children.textRawHtml: You can’t leave is hanging like that!  What happened?
children.textZhHtml:
你不能就这么挂着！ 发生了什么？
奇怪的是，在我的国家，我们有一种文化，科学家们喜欢互相追逐——这就是他们生存的目的！没有什么比破坏他人的声誉更能给你带来名声的了。

推翻信念会让你直接载入史册。人们以重做 90 年代的案件为生，这太荒谬了。

美国有无数的联邦起诉，其内容类似于

1）大量证据表明某人有罪。

2）联邦“专家证人”允许并资助作证指向X人

3）辩护失败

4）如果辩护没有失败，法官会找到辩护专家证人无法提供完整证据的原因论点

5）检方提出认罪协议，否则将被判入狱数亿年

6）当一个人意识到自己的辩护不被允许或不会得到资助时，他们就会放弃，或者接受审判，并因敢于接受审判而被判数亿年。

如果你已经拥有一堆犯罪证据和专家证人，你可以继续堆放，将其扔给某个随机的人并不是一件容易的事，正如我们所见在这里，实际上很简单。

推翻定罪假定被告被错误定罪，并且科学家具有与案件相关的技术技能。

问题在于，这些交叉条件使得相关案件的数量很少，而在普通案件中让专家以低廉的价格为被告作证的要求更高。

如果您不介意的话，那是哪个国家/地区？
我听检察官说过，无罪或有罪并不重要。 重要的是他们能否定罪。
“Clair Obscur：Expedition 33”是一款法国游戏（用户名为 expedition 32），这听起来像是法国人会喜欢的游戏，所以我想到的是法国，但我只是假设。

children.author: mothballed
children.textRawHtml:
There are a gazillion federal prosecutions in the US that go something like

1) Pile of evidence that someone is guilty.

2) Federal "expert witness" allowed and funded to testify it points to X person

3) Defense is broke

4) If defense not broke, judge finds reason why defense expert witness can't present their full argument

5) Prosecution offers plea deal or a gazillion years in jail

6) Person folds when they realize none of their defense is allowed or will be funded, or goes to trial and gets a gazillion years for daring to go to trial.

If you already have a pile of evidence for a crime and an expert witnesses you can keep piling on it's not much of a stretch to dump it on some random person, as we saw here, quite easy actually.
children.textZhHtml:
美国有无数的联邦起诉，其内容类似于

1）大量证据表明某人有罪。

2）联邦“专家证人”允许并资助作证指向X人

3）辩护失败

4）如果辩护没有失败，法官会找到辩护专家证人无法提供完整证据的原因论点

5）检方提出认罪协议，否则将被判入狱数亿年

6）当一个人意识到自己的辩护不被允许或不会得到资助时，他们就会放弃，或者接受审判，并因敢于接受审判而被判数亿年。

如果你已经拥有一堆犯罪证据和专家证人，你可以继续堆放，将其扔给某个随机的人并不是一件容易的事，正如我们所见在这里，实际上很简单。

children.author: voakbasda
children.textRawHtml: I have heard prosecutors say that innocent or guilty doesn’t matter.  All that matters is whether they can convict.
children.textZhHtml: 我听检察官说过，无罪或有罪并不重要。  重要的是他们能否定罪。

children.author: qingcharles
children.textRawHtml:
I've known and hung out with a lot of prosecutors. I've never heard one say anything like that outright, but, one of the main issues is that in 99.9% of cases the evidence will not be looked at. They are just not given the time and resources to even take a single glance at the police reports, never mind any forensic evidence. They literally have no idea whether the person is guilty or innocent when they offer a plea deal.

Even your paid defense attorney might never look at the case files at all. Jared from Subway's lawyer got into hot water because he got Jared to take a plea and it turned out he was factually innocent of one of the many offenses he was charged with, and that fact would have been uncovered quickly had the defense attorney ever looked at the evidence, which he said he had not.
children.textZhHtml:
我认识不少检察官，也跟他们打过交道。我从来没听谁这么直白地说过，但是，一个主要问题是，在99.9%的案件中，证据根本不会被审查。他们根本没有时间和资源去哪怕扫一眼警方报告，更别提什么法医证据了。他们在提出认罪协议时，完全不知道当事人是有罪还是无辜。

就连你花钱请的辩护律师可能也根本不看案卷。赛百味贾里德的律师就惹了麻烦，因为他让贾里德认了罪，结果发现贾里德在多项指控中有一项事实上是无辜的，而且如果辩护律师看过证据，这个事实很快就能查清，但他承认自己根本没看过证据。

children.author: thephyber
children.textRawHtml: In the US legal system, the defense isn't given access to the prosecution's evidence used in the case immediately. In fact, lots of plea bargains happen before the defense attorney knows for sure what evidence there is to tie their client to the crime.
children.textZhHtml: 在美国司法体系中，辩护方并不能立即获取控方在案件中使用的证据。事实上，很多认罪协商都是在辩护律师还不确定有哪些证据能将他们的当事人与犯罪联系起来之前就已经达成了。

children.author: qingcharles
children.textRawHtml:
Absolutely. Defense usually has to file a motion, then god forbid the evidence is something like an obscure-format security video; nobody will ever figure out how to get it to the defense or how to play it back.

Most plea bargains are done simply based on the charging instruments.
children.textZhHtml:
完全正确。辩方通常必须提交动议，然后要是证据是某种冷门格式的安全监控视频，那可就麻烦了；根本没人知道怎么把视频交给辩方，也没人知道怎么播放。

大多数认罪协商仅仅是基于控告文书进行的。

children.author: thephyber
children.textRawHtml:
I doubt any professional prosecutors would say this out loud. This is likely a disciplinable or disbarrable statement.

This is effectively a truth, but prosecutors are generally held to high ethical standards, where they are expected to drop cases / not bring cases if the evidence doesn't point specifically to the defendant.

That said, there are occasionally times when prosecutors have been caught hiding / burying / not sharing exculpatory evidence (something the police / prosecution found which would help the defense's case against the prosecution). The only reason to do so would be to sandbag the case against the defendant even when there is a shadow of a doubt in the prosecution's case.
children.textZhHtml:
我怀疑没有任何职业检察官会公开这么说。这很可能是要受纪律处分甚至被吊销执照的言论。

但这实际上是个事实，不过检察官通常被要求遵守较高的职业道德标准，如果证据不能明确指向被告，他们理应撤销案件或不予起诉。

话虽如此，偶尔也会有检察官被发现隐瞒、掩盖或不移交开脱证据（即警方或控方发现的有助于辩方对抗控方的证据）。这么做唯一的目的就是在控方案件尚存疑点时，也要暗中算计被告。

children.author: expedition32
children.textRawHtml:
Weird in my country we have a culture were scientists love going after eachother- its what they live for! Nothing gives you more fame than destroying other people's reputation.

And overturning convictions gets you straight into the history books. It gets so ridiculous that people make their life work out of redoing cases from the 90s.
children.textZhHtml:
奇怪的是，在我的国家，我们有一种文化，科学家们喜欢互相追逐——这就是他们生存的目的！没有什么比破坏他人的声誉更能给你带来名声的了。

推翻信念会让你直接载入史册。人们以重做 90 年代的案件为生，这太荒谬了。

children.author: thephyber
children.textRawHtml:
Overturning convictions presumes that the defendant was wrongfully convicted and that the scientist has the technical skill which is relevant in the case.

The problem is that these intersecting conditions make the number of relevant cases small, while having experts testify for defendants for cheap during mundane cases has MUCH higher demand.
children.textZhHtml:
推翻定罪假定被告被错误定罪，并且科学家具有与案件相关的技术技能。

问题在于，这些交叉条件使得相关案件的数量很少，而在普通案件中让专家以低廉的价格为被告作证的要求更高。

Canadian justice system is under stronge pressure to bring rate of conviction up. Only 0.001% rapist end in prison and bs like that.

Some corners must be cut, to reach quotas!

stories.title: Apple Will 'Watch Everything Burn' When the AI Bubble Bursts
stories.titleZh: 当AI泡沫破裂时，苹果将“坐视一切灰飞烟灭”

comments.author: cmiles8
comments.textRawHtml:
Apple looks better and better as every day passes. Other players going deeply into debt to build out massive infrastructure, VCs pumping up the model ecosystem that is now a total commodity.

Apple’s just been sitting there with solid cashflow waiting for all this to implode and then have on-device models with their own chips.

Apple will own the end device while the rest of the world is fighting over a pure commodity. It will burn hard and Apple will laugh all the way to the bank.
comments.textZhHtml:
随着时间一天天过去，Apple 看起来越来越好。其他参与者深陷债务以建设大规模基础设施，风投则推动了模型生态系统的发展，而模型生态系统现在已经成为一种商品。

苹果只是坐在那里，拥有稳定的现金流，等待这一切崩溃，然后拥有带有自己芯片的设备模型。

当世界其他国家正在争夺纯粹的商品时，苹果将拥有终端设备。它会燃烧得很厉害，苹果会一路笑到银行。

children.author: throwaway63467
children.textRawHtml: Isn’t Apple potentially under a lot of pressure due to the DRAM prices as well as having to compete with AI for fab capacity? Before all the price hikes their products were already priced at the top of the market so I would assume that memory getting more expensive will impact their sales or margin quite a bit as they can’t subsidize hardware like AI companies do (they can of course eat into their own margins a bit which I think they already do). So not sure if what happens right now is great for them, if the memory market collapses it will of course be good.
children.textZhHtml: 由于 DRAM 价格以及必须与 AI 竞争晶圆厂产能，苹果是否面临很大压力？在所有价格上涨之前，他们的产品定价已经处于市场顶部，因此我认为内存变得更加昂贵将会对他们的销售或利润产生相当大的影响，因为他们无法像人工智能公司那样补贴硬件（他们当然可以稍微蚕食自己的利润，我认为他们已经这样做了）。所以不确定现在发生的事情对他们来说是否有利，如果内存市场崩溃那当然是好事。

children.author: alpha_squared
children.textRawHtml:
> Isn’t Apple potentially under a lot of pressure due to the DRAM prices as well as having to compete with AI for fab capacity?

I'd qualify this with for now. It's not entirely clear what happens in the event the AI industry implodes, but I do think there will be a glut of memory and hardware up for grabs. It very well could crash the consumer hardware market as a result. The AI obsession and investment has burrowed so deeply across the US economy that I can't think of a single industry that won't be impacted, including agriculture.
children.textZhHtml:
> 由于 DRAM 价格以及必须与 AI 竞争晶圆厂产能，苹果是否会面临巨大压力？

我暂时用来限定这一点。目前尚不完全清楚如果人工智能行业崩溃会发生什么，但我确实认为将会出现大量内存和硬件可供争夺。结果很可能会导致消费硬件市场崩溃。对人工智能的痴迷和投资已经深入美国经济，我想不出有哪个行业不会受到影响，包括农业。

children.author: thewebguyd
children.textRawHtml:
> It very well could crash the consumer hardware market as a result

Tbh, I hope it does. Prices are outrageous, and I'm a firm believer in personal computing/having access to powerful hardware, privately and locally, is hugely important.

On a more selfish note, I miss the days of being able to build an outrageously powerful desktop for myself for relatively cheap. For now I'm still holding onto my AM4 motherboard w/ 64GB DDR4 and an aging GPU, praying my 7 y/o GPU holds up long enough for prices to drop again.
children.textZhHtml:
> 这很可能会导致消费硬件市场崩溃

说实话，我希望如此。价格高得离谱，而且我坚信个人计算/私下和本地访问强大的硬件非常重要。

更自私的是，我怀念能够以相对便宜的价格为自己构建功能强大的桌面的日子。目前，我仍然保留着配备 64GB DDR4 的 AM4 主板和老化的 GPU，祈祷我的 7 岁 GPU 能够坚持足够长的时间，以便价格再次下跌。

children.author: bpavuk
children.textRawHtml: 64 GB! you are lucky :) sitting there with 16GB, a GPU that already shows the signs of strain, and AM4 Ryzen 5 5600G. (MacBook Air M1 equivalent in single-threaded tasks.) apparently the CPU requirements slowly crept up across the line. and then there is looming AVX512. why "looming"? because at some point enough people will move to it that software will require AVX512.
children.textZhHtml: 64 GB！你很幸运:) 坐在那里，拥有 16GB、已经显示出压力迹象的 GPU 和 AM4 Ryzen 5 5600G。 （MacBook Air M1 相当于单线程任务。）显然 CPU 要求慢慢地越过了界限。还有即将出现的AVX512。为何“若隐若现”？因为在某个时候会有足够多的人转向该软件，因此软件将需要 AVX512。

children.author: Someone
children.textRawHtml:
> Isn’t Apple potentially under a lot of pressure due to the DRAM prices

Maybe. On the one hand, if there is a strong ceiling to what users are willing/able to pay for a smartphone (might not be true, with all those people making $$ on the stock market), they will have to cut prices.

On the other hand, if one part gets more expensive, premium phones need smaller relative price increases than budget phones. Certainly, if they are willing to accept lower margins, premium product might get more attractive.

Also, iPhones tend to have less RAM than competitors, so this might hit other premium manufacturers harder than Apple.
children.textZhHtml:
> 苹果是否会因 DRAM 价格而承受很大压力

也许吧。一方面，如果用户愿意/能够为智能手机支付的费用有一个严格的上限（可能不是真的，因为所有这些人都在股市上赚钱），他们将不得不降价。

另一方面，如果一个零件变得更贵，高端手机需要比廉价手机更小的相对价格上涨。当然，如果他们愿意接受较低的利润，高端产品可能会更具吸引力。

此外，iPhone 的 RAM 往往比竞争对手少，因此这可能会对其他高端制造商造成比苹果更大的打击。

children.author: cmiles8
children.textRawHtml: Yes it does impact all hardware makers and they raised prices as a result. But again remember the financial reality here… DRAM is in short supply because of the demand for models propped up by VC subsidies and infrastructure providers going deeply into debt to buy all this stuff just as folks are realizing we’re on track to over build capacity. So yes Apple gets impacted a bit in the short term but in the long term they’ll gleefully watch it all burn.
children.textZhHtml: 是的，这确实影响了所有硬件制造商，他们因此提高了价格。但请再次记住这里的财务现实……DRAM 供不应求，因为对由风险投资补贴支撑的模型的需求以及基础设施提供商深陷债务购买所有这些东西，就像人们意识到我们正在过度建设产能一样。所以，是的，苹果在短期内会受到一些影响，但从长远来看，他们会高兴地看着它全部燃烧。

children.author: CoolestBeans
children.textRawHtml:
Sure, but DRAM is a commodity and is classically cyclical. This is a particularly large cycle but so long as the historic pattern holds (and there's not a ton of reason to think it won't unless the hyperscalars can go into greater debt indefinitely which given inflation and interest rates they can't) Apple just needs to get through this peak in prices, which they have a LOT of ammunition to do so.

Having to raise prices isn't a great look but when they come out the other side they can drop pirces and get a boost in volume or they can keep them high and enjoy a bigger profit margin.
children.textZhHtml: 当然，但 DRAM 是一种商品，并且具有典型的周期性。这是一个特别大的周期，但只要历史模式保持不变（没有太多理由认为它不会，除非超标量可以无限期地陷入更大的债务，而考虑到通货膨胀和利率，他们不能）苹果只需要度过这个价格峰值，他们有很多弹药来做到这一点。他们可以保持较高的利润并享受更大的利润率。
